summary: Lifecycle walk, run live in the dev container (CLI built from release/6.1.0 @007473ad, reports 6.0.0). I created a marketplace in $TMPDIR/pkglc-market with `yg marketplace init` and `yg pack new house-style`, then added a prose aspect (tone) and a deterministic aspect that imports a helper module (banned/check.mjs importing ./lib.mjs). I tagged 0.1.0 to 0.5.0, plus an untagged 0.6.0 on HEAD. Installs went into $TMPDIR/pkglc-proj* from a local path (with --as), with a pinned version (@0.1.0), and from a file-scheme git URL. I then attached the rules, ran check and --approve --only-deterministic, edited and removed copied files, updated (no-arg, named, --to, rollback), renamed a config key upstream, ran drills, and removed the package. What works: adapt carry-over, invalidation when a config value changes, refusal of an edited copy, refusal of unknown files, and the advise nomination. Where it breaks: (a) cached verdicts survive a package update that changes a rule's imported helper; (b) the documented identity, pinning and tag models do not match the code; (c) the error hints send users into dead ends; (d) running `yg pack` from a subdirectory writes a stray install; (e) drills cannot run any rule shaped like the scaffold.

surviving.title: A pinned install is not sticky: bare `yg pack update` moves it to whatever HEAD's manifest says
surviving.where: docs/packages.md:32-36 ('Pin a version by adding it'); source/cli/src/cli/pack.ts:798-806; lock entry has no pin/ref field (package-store.ts renderPackagesLock)

summary:
Code-correctness audit of the package system on release/6.1.0. The package code (source/cli/src/cli/pack.ts, io/package-store.ts, io/package-manifest-parser.ts, core/checks/packages.ts, utils/git-pack-fetch.ts, the package branch of core/graph-loader.ts and io/aspect-parser.ts) has not changed since v6.0.0, so everything below affects the shipped 6.0.0 and the upcoming 6.1.0 alike. I reproduced every behavioural finding with the live dev-container CLI in scratch projects under $TMPDIR/pkcc*. The only exceptions are the rename-after-rm window in F7 and the UTF-8 round trip in F10, which come from reading the code.

Most serious:
- F1: a crafted `package:` value in the lock makes `yg pack remove` delete the whole project, .git included. Reproduced.
- F2: helper modules that check.mjs imports are left out of the verdict hash. A package update that changes only a helper therefore keeps a stale PASS, while a fresh run refuses the same code.
- F3: the CLI writes log.md into an installed package's copy, and its own package-file-modified rail then fails `yg check`.

The docs contradict the code in three places:
- Same-named packages from two publishers are said to install side by side. The lock is keyed by the bare name, so the second install is refused.
- `update` has no attachment guard, so a renamed or dropped rule leaves dangling references and the adaptations for it are lost.
- Version handling is loose: silent downgrades, and a tag whose manifest says a different version is recorded under the manifest's number.

Correct as far as I checked: marketplace path traversal (lexical escapesRoot), symlinks inside a package (refused through lstat), undeclared top-level directories, git argument injection (execFile with `--`), identity segment validation, the drift refusal before any replacement, and the lock `files:` prefix check.

Incident during setup: my scratch setup script ran `git config --global` inside the container and overwrote user.name/user.email. It also added init.defaultBranch. I restored user.name and user.email to the identity seen on the container's commits and removed the added [init] section. If other agents made commits in that short window, they may carry the author "t <t@t>".

surviving.title: Lock `package:` is never validated; `yg pack remove` (and `update`) will rm -rf outside .yggdrasil/aspects/packages — deleted the whole project root including .git
surviving.where: source/cli/src/io/package-manifest-parser.ts:551-552 (installId taken verbatim), 572 (only files: entries are checked); source/cli/src/io/package-store.ts:367-370 (removePackageFiles), 233-234 + 304 (installPackage rm(finalAbs)); source/cli/src/cli/pack.ts:965
surviving.evidence: parsePackagesLock does `const installId = (entry.package as string).trim();` with no segment/escape check; the escape check only runs per files: key, so `files: {}` skips it entirely. Repro: copied a consumer to $TMPDIR/pkcc/victim/proj, appended to .yggdrasil/yg-packages.yaml a record `"helper": {source: https://github.com/acme/helper.git, package: "../../..", version: 1.0.0, installed_at: ..., files: {}}`. `yg pack list` printed `helper 1.0.0 copy untouched ... at .yggdrasil/aspects/packages/../../../`. `yg pack remove helper` printed `Removed 'helper' — its rules and its record are gone.` exit=0, and `ls -la $TMPDIR/pkcc/victim/proj` then showed only `.yggdrasil` (recreated by the lock write). src/, .git and everything else were gone. `update` on the same record would reach `rm(finalAbs, {recursive:true})` at package-store.ts:304 on the same resolved path.
surviving.impact: The lock is a committed, reviewable-looking file. A one-line change in a PR, or a hand-merged lock conflict, turns a routine `yg pack remove`/`update` into recursive deletion of the repository, .git included, with a success message. The attachment guard does not help: a fake entry has no attachments.
surviving.suggested_fix: In parsePackagesLock, require `package` to be exactly three isSingleSegment parts (owner/repo/name), matching `name` as the third segment. Also add a containment assertion in removePackageFiles/installPackage: path.resolve(target) must start with path.resolve(aspects/packages) + sep, otherwise refuse. summary: Trust and security review of the package system on release/6.1.0. I read docs/packages.md, the packages-and-marketplaces knowledge topic, cli/pack.ts, io/package-store.ts, io/package-manifest-parser.ts, core/checks/packages.ts, core/pair-inputs.ts, core/fill.ts and core/log/aspect-status.ts. I then ran the dev-container CLI (dist 6.0.0 build of release/6.1.0) against scratch marketplaces and consumers under $TMPDIR/sectrust-* (since removed). Several things hold up: a check.mjs that writes $TMPDIR/sectrust-pwned.txt and reads process.env does run during fill, as the danger box admits. Git is called with argv only. Symlinks, binaries and marketplace path escapes are refused. `yg marketplace check` did not execute the package's code. The weak points are elsewhere. (1) Verdict freshness: a deterministic verdict hashes only check.mjs bytes, so a package update that changes only a helper module keeps a stale PASS. (2) The committed yg-packages.yaml is fully trusted input: its `package` install id is never validated (a crafted entry made `yg pack remove` rm -rf a directory outside .yggdrasil), its `source` can be redirected while the trusted identity stays put, and its hashes can be rewritten along with the copy. (3) Updates silently escalate authority: the adapt stub pins config defaults but not status, so a package can move draft→enforced and pull in brand-new implied rules whose code then runs on --approve. (4) The CLI's own status-change log writes log.md into the installed copy, and the drift rail then blocks the repo with "a rule nobody chose". (5) Provenance: install without a version takes the default branch HEAD or an uncommitted local working tree, and records the manifest's claimed version with no tag or commit SHA. The docs' claim that same-named packages from two repositories install side by side is false: the lock is keyed by bare name.

summary:
Model-and-docs review of the package system on release/6.1.0 (package code unchanged since v6.0.0: `git log v6.0.0..HEAD` over pack.ts, package-store.ts, checks/packages.ts, marketplace-check.ts and package-manifest-parser.ts is empty, so everything below shipped in 6.0.0). I read docs/packages.md, the packages-and-marketplaces knowledge topic, cli-reference (docs and knowledge), configuration.md, family-contracts.md, CHANGELOG, the model, the store, the drift rail, fetch, and the advise feed and tests. I also ran the live CLI in scratch projects under $TMPDIR/pkgmodel-* in the container.

The copy-and-adapt idea holds up: the drift rail, the adapt merge and atomic install are careful and well tested on a single package from a single source in the repo root. The model breaks in four places:
- **Where it runs from.** Every `yg pack` subcommand except `new` treats the current directory as the project root.
- **Identity.** Installed packages are recorded by bare name, which contradicts the promise that two repositories' same-named packages install side by side.
- **Versions.** A pinned version is never remembered, and a plain add or update takes the source's default-branch HEAD. So `update` can silently downgrade, and the advise/list notices point at a command that does not take the version they advertise.
- **Multi-package operations.** An update over several packages applies partially and then claims nothing changed.

Settings interact badly with updates. The stub pins every key, so renaming or removing a setting breaks every consumer at load. Docs contradict themselves on update atomicity. `requires.yg` is open-ended and checked only once. Sources are stored verbatim in a committed file. Tests cover none of these paths.
